question: What is the declared range of the NOVA-3 1.0 L Dedicated CNG variant?
gold_answer: 310 km (CNG only, combined cycle). The Dedicated CNG variant has no petrol reserve tank, so nothing is added to this figure.
notes: Adjacent Bi-fuel column reads 220 (CNG) + 195 (petrol reserve) km; Appendix A has 326 km for Dedicated (Rev C). Row is in a transposed table.

question: What is the maximum power of the NOVA-3 Bi-fuel CNG variant?
gold_answer: 40.2 kW @ 6000 rpm (CNG operation, the declared rating). The 50.1 kW @ 6000 rpm figure is petrol-reserve mode only and must not be quoted as the rating.
notes: Footnote a changes the meaning of the value; Dedicated CNG column has 44.5 kW @ 6200 rpm.

question: What is the braked towing capacity of the ATLAS-6 Dedicated CNG Double-Cab?
gold_answer: 2,000 kg (diesel variants: 2,500 kg).
notes: Shares engine family D20C with the diesels but towing is lower; footnote b. TERRA-9 Turbo Petrol also has 2,000 kg (near-duplicate across documents).

question: What maximum power and torque does the TERRA-9 2.2 L Diesel Mild-Hybrid AT deliver from the engine alone, i.e. with the 48 V system inactive?
gold_answer: Engine-only: 118 kW @ 3750 rpm and 380 N·m @ 1750-2500 rpm (identical to the non-hybrid Diesel AT). The 125 kW / 400 N·m system-combined figures apply only with the 48 V system charged and active.
notes: Footnote a; combined figure is the tempting answer. Header of last column wraps over two lines in extracted text.

question: How far can the ZENITH-11 Plug-in Hybrid travel on electricity alone?
gold_answer: 72 km (electric-only range, Revision B). Not the 1,050 km combined range or the 640 km engine-only range.
notes: Three range rows for one variant; footnote c explicitly warns. Rev A value 64 km is in Appendix A. Page 2 quick-reference table also states 72 km (accepted as a citation).

question: For the VOLTA-4 Performance AWD, what are the usable battery capacity and the declared combined range?
gold_answer: Usable capacity 58.0 kWh (gross 62.0 kWh is a manufacturing figure only); declared combined range 418 km.
notes: Long Range has the same 58.0 kWh usable but 452 km range; gross vs usable trap; kWh vs kW.

question: What is the compression ratio of the NOVA-3 Dedicated CNG engine, and may it be run on petrol?
gold_answer: 12.5 : 1. No - the Dedicated CNG engine must not be fuelled with petrol under any circumstances (detonation damage, not covered by warranty). The Bi-fuel CNG variant is 10.5 : 1.
notes: Footnote c; Bi-fuel and Petrol columns are 10.5:1.

question: What is the declared CNG-only range of the NOVA-3 Bi-fuel CNG variant?
gold_answer: 220 km on CNG (plus 195 km on the petrol reserve, shown separately and not additive). The earlier 238 km figure was superseded at Revision D.
notes: Naive-answer trap: Appendix A (p13) shows 238 km for Bi-fuel and looks like current data.

question: What is the declared driving range of the VEGA-7 Bi-fuel CNG variant?
gold_answer: 298 km (CNG operation only, excludes the reserve petrol tank), per Revision C. The 310 km figure is the superseded Revision B value.
notes: Appendix A (p14) table A.1 shows 310 km. Naive retrieval of the appendix gives the wrong answer.

question: What was the VOLTA-4 Long Range DC fast-charge 10-80% time under the previous revision (Revision B), before it was changed?
gold_answer: 42 minutes (Revision B). This is superseded: Revision C (22 Jan 2026) corrected it to 38 minutes. The answer should be labelled as superseded.
notes: Explicitly asks for the superseded value; must come from Appendix A and be labelled superseded, not refused and not presented as current.

question: What was the ATLAS-6 Dedicated CNG payload before it was corrected to 1,230 kg?
gold_answer: 1,260 kg (superseded). It was corrected to 1,230 kg after a revised axle load test (change recorded at Revision E, 12 Aug 2025; Appendix A labels the 1,260 kg value as Revision D).
notes: Asks for the superseded value; answer from Appendix A and label as superseded. Dossier is internally loose about which revision (E in history, D in Appendix A, F column in quick reference).

question: What is the scheduled brake-fluid replacement interval for the VEGA-7?
gold_answer: 36 months (Revision C, for vehicles built from 01 March 2026). The 48-month interval is the superseded Revision B value.
notes: Appendix A table A.2 shows 48 months for all variants. Brake-fluid interval is also 36 months on NOVA-3 (extended from 24 at Rev C) - a cross-document near-duplicate.

question: What part number is the NOVA-3 rear shock absorber lower bush at Revision D?
gold_answer: The Revision D change record (p2) says the rear shock absorber lower bush changed from 3382-A to 3382-C. However, Section 4 and Appendix A identify 3382-C / 3382-A as the rear crossmember bracket, not a bush. The documents are inconsistent on what component 3382-x is; the answer should state 3382-C per the change record and flag the inconsistency.
notes: Genuine internal inconsistency in the source (bush vs bracket). A system that silently answers 3382-C without noting the conflict should be marked down.

question: What is the front spring rate of the VEGA-7 1.0 L Turbo Petrol, and what condition applies to the figure?
gold_answer: 24.1 N/mm. The quoted rates are for the production bracket 4471-C; vehicles built before 01 March 2026 with bracket 4471-A have an effective front rate 1.8 N/mm lower (22.3 N/mm).
notes: Value is in the third of four columns; footnote c qualifies it. Appendix A (p14) lists 22.3 for Rev B Turbo Petrol; the 22.3 in the gold answer is derived from the footnote and equals that.

question: What are the kerb mass and gross vehicle mass of the TERRA-9 2.2 L Diesel Mild-Hybrid AT?
gold_answer: Kerb mass 1960 kg; gross vehicle mass 2650 kg.
notes: Fourth column of a four-variant transposed table; header wraps. Diesel AT is 1895/2580, Turbo Petrol 1790/2470.

question: For the VOLTA-4 Performance AWD, what are the DC fast-charge peak power, the DC 10-80% time and the AC onboard charger power?
gold_answer: DC fast charge peak 150 kW; 10-80% in 32 minutes (assumes active battery preconditioning); AC onboard charger 11.0 kW.
notes: Third column; Long Range is 120 kW / 38 min / 11.0 kW; Standard Range 50 kW / 55 min / 7.2 kW. Footnote c on preconditioning.

question: What is the cold front tyre pressure for the ATLAS-6 2.0 L Diesel Double-Cab?
gold_answer: 310 kPa (laden). Single-Cab 300 kPa; Dedicated CNG Double-Cab 320 kPa.
notes: Second column; row label says 'laden'. Neighbouring columns differ by only 10 kPa.

question: Which tests in the VEGA-7 homologation log are CMVR 115A tests, and how many are there?
gold_answer: 5 tests: HOM-033 (CNG cylinder burst margin), HOM-034 (CNG line leak, 1.5x service), HOM-035 (CNG PRD activation temp.) on page 7, and HOM-062 (CNG filling receptacle, cycles) and HOM-063 (CNG cylinder mounting, 20 g) on page 8.
notes: Exhaustive list across a 3-page table. HOM-036 (CNG methane emission) is a CNG test but under AIS-137 Pt.4, not CMVR 115A.

question: Which tests in the VEGA-7 homologation log have the result Fail, and what were the measured values against the limits?
gold_answer: 3 failures: HOM-017 door latch, longitudinal load (limit >=11.0 kN, measured 9.80 kN) on page 6; HOM-029 pedestrian head, adult zone (limit <=1000 HIC, measured 1086.0 HIC) and HOM-038 roof crush, second stage (limit >=1.50 ratio, measured 1.41) on page 7. The two Cond. Pass results (HOM-066, HOM-068) are not failures.
notes: Exhaustive; pages 6-7 (summary Table 3.2 on p8 confirms count of 3). Cond. Pass and N/A must not be counted as Fail.

question: For VEGA-7 test HOM-056 (ISOFIX lower anchor pull), what are the limit, measured value, unit, result and report?
gold_answer: Limit >=8.00, measured 10.90, unit kN, result Pass, report ER-2434.
notes: Row is on page 8 which carries no column headings; headings are on page 6 only. Needs header re-association.

question: In the NOVA-3 homologation log, which tests are documented under report ER-3104?
gold_answer: 4 tests: HOM-005 (CNG system gas-tightness), HOM-006 (PRD function test), HOM-007 (CNG cylinder burst pressure, 612.0 bar) on page 6, and HOM-033 (CNG cylinder cyclic pressure fatigue, 22400 cycles) on page 7.
notes: Exhaustive filter on the Report column across a 2-page table. HOM-034 (CNG shutoff valve) is ER-3105, not ER-3104.

question: Did any TERRA-9 homologation test fail? If so, which, and what is the status?
gold_answer: Yes, one: HOM-022 pedestrian head, adult zone (limit <=1000 HIC, measured 1042.0 HIC, report ER-4538) on page 6. The failure is on the Turbo Petrol bonnet profile only; concession granted pending bonnet liner re-test ER-4538R (totals line on page 7: 43 Pass, 1 Fail of 44).
notes: Result row and the qualifying totals note are on different pages. 'See Appendix A' in the totals line is a dangling reference.

question: How many of the VOLTA-4 homologation tests failed, and how many passed?
gold_answer: 0 failed; 38 of 38 passed (the log spans pages 6-7; totals line on page 7).
notes: Negative/complete count over a 2-page table. Do not confuse with VEGA-7 (68 tests, 3 fail) or NOVA-3 (42 tests, 1 fail).

question: A VEGA-7 Bi-fuel CNG is operated at an ambient temperature of 40.5 degC. What range correction applies and what is the corrected declared range?
gold_answer: 40.5 degC is above 40 degC, so the 'Above 40 up to 48 degC' band applies: range -6 %. Corrected range = 298 km x 0.94 = about 280 km (computed from the current Revision C figure of 298 km, not the superseded 310 km).
notes: Band boundaries are inclusive of the upper bound (exactly 40 degC would be -3 %); the page states the 40.5 example explicitly. Correction applies to the current declared figure, not Appendix A.

question: What range, power and service-interval corrections apply to the NOVA-3 at an ambient temperature of 45 degC?
gold_answer: Declared range -5 %, declared power -4 %, service interval -20 % (band 'Above 40 up to 48 degC'). Altitude corrections, if any, are cumulative and separate.
notes: Other documents have different percentages for the same band (e.g. TERRA-9 range -6 %, power -6 %, towing -10 %; VEGA-7 range -6 %, power -5 %).

question: What is the transmission-fluid replacement interval for the TERRA-9 1.5 L Turbo Petrol AT?
gold_answer: 60,000 km (time interval 96 months). The table's default distance of 80,000 km applies to the Diesel MT/AT and Mild-Hybrid AT variants.
notes: A variant column cell overrides the row default distance. Yes/value cells mix. Also the same row in VEGA-7 has 60,000 km for the Turbo petrol.

question: How much does the ZENITH-11 Plug-in Hybrid's electric-only range reduce at an ambient temperature of 45 degC, and what is the resulting range?
gold_answer: Electric-only range correction for 'Above 40 up to 48 degC' is -10 %, so 72 km x 0.90 = about 64.8 km. (Note this is a computed value; it is not the superseded Revision A figure of 64 km.)
notes: Electric-only column is separate from the declared range column (-5 % in that band). Result 64.8 is numerically close to the Rev A 64 km trap.

question: On the VOLTA-4 battery degradation claim flow, a claim is made within 8 years / 160,000 km. The measured SOH is 68 % of rated and the degradation is within the fleet norm band. What is the outcome?
gold_answer: No fault found (claim closed, no pack replacement). Path: within coverage -> measured SOH < 70 % of rated = Yes -> degradation within fleet norm band = Yes -> No fault found. Pack replacement (A-14) happens only if degradation is faster than the norm band.
notes: Requires tracing the decision flow (Figure 6.1). Superseded threshold was 65 % (at 68 % the Rev B path would have been 'No fault found' immediately).

question: A ZENITH-11 HV battery claim has a measured state of health of 64 % of rated usable capacity. What outcome code does the adjudication flow give?
gold_answer: A-33 - referred to the Technical Committee for review (SOH below 70 % of rated). At or above 70 % the claim closes with no fault found.
notes: HV branch bypasses the 3 yr/100,000 km test. TERRA-9 has a different HV branch (5 yr unlimited km, SOH grading per Table 8.2a not given).

question: On an ATLAS-6 pickup that was operated above its gross vehicle mass at the time of failure, a claim is made on a covered part, 2 years after registration and well inside 100,000 km. What is the outcome?
gold_answer: Rejected under code R-21 (GVM exceeded at time of failure). The overload test is applied first and takes precedence over every other outcome, even for an otherwise covered part.
notes: First decision node in Figure 6.1; ATLAS-6 flow differs from the other dossiers (coverage is not the first test).

question: A NOVA-3 vehicle is 1 year old with 15,000 km. A claim is raised for a part that is not a wear item, with a claim value of INR 20,000. What is the outcome?
gold_answer: Referred to the Technical Committee for review - outcome code A-33 (15 working days). Within 2 yr/40,000 km, not a wear item, and INR 20,000 exceeds the INR 15,000 threshold.
notes: Needs the claim-value diamond in Figure 6.1. VEGA-7 threshold is INR 25,000 (would be auto-approved A-02 there).

question: In the VEGA-7 front strut assembly figure, which callout number is the highlighted (orange-red) component, what is it, and what tightening torque and angle apply to it?
gold_answer: Callout 7, the lower-arm mounting bracket (part 4471-C): 110 +/- 10 N.m plus a 45 degree angle stage, single use. (The superseded 4471-A was 95 N.m with no angle.)
notes: The highlight colour is only visible in the drawing; mapping callout -> torque row needs the figure caption and Table 4.1 together.

question: In TERRA-9 Figure 4.1 (third-row seat mechanism), which two callout boxes are drawn highlighted in orange, and what components are they?
gold_answer: Callout 3 (recline latch) and callout 8 (seat belt buckle anchor).
notes: Purely visual attribute (no legend explains the highlight); answerable only by looking at the image. The caption says item 3 is the part revised at Revision E; 8 is highlighted too.

question: What is the ex-showroom retail price of the NOVA-3 Dedicated CNG?
notes: Dossiers contain only component unit costs (Table 5.2), never vehicle prices.

question: What are the HV battery state-of-health grading thresholds in TERRA-9 Table 8.2a?
notes: Table 8.2a is explicitly not reproduced in the dossier (refers to NM-COR-WR-0002, not in the corpus). The question has a real referent but no data.

question: What is the top speed of the ZENITH-11 Plug-in Hybrid in electric-only mode?
notes: Only the overall maximum speed (225 km/h) is given; no electric-only speed. Tempting to answer with 225.

question: What is the kerb mass of the NOVA-3 export configuration?
notes: Scope section (p3) says the export configuration is documented separately; not in the corpus. Tempting to answer with the domestic kerb mass.

question: What is the spark-plug replacement interval for the NOVA-3 CNG variant?
gold_answer: Needs clarification: NOVA-3 has two CNG variants. Bi-fuel CNG: 40,000 km (unchanged at Rev D); Dedicated CNG: 20,000 km (Rev D; was 30,000 km).
notes: Variant unspecified, answers differ by factor 2. Superseded 30,000 km adds a second trap.

question: What is the warranty coverage period for a claim?
gold_answer: Needs clarification of platform (and for TERRA-9/ZENITH-11 whether it is an HV battery claim): NOVA-3 2 years/40,000 km; ATLAS-6, TERRA-9 (non-HV), VEGA-7 and ZENITH-11 (non-HV) 3 years/100,000 km; TERRA-9 HV battery/control module 5 years unlimited km; VOLTA-4 battery degradation 8 years/160,000 km.
notes: No platform given; the correct behaviour is to ask which vehicle rather than pick one. NOVA-3 explicitly warns it differs from VEGA-7.

question: What is the kerb mass of the 2.2 L Diesel AT?
gold_answer: Needs clarification: TERRA-9 2.2 L Diesel AT is 1895 kg; ZENITH-11 2.2 L Diesel AT is 1760 kg.
notes: Same variant name and shared H22D engine family on two platforms; platform unspecified.

question: Which is the most powerful variant among the Northwind motor cars?
gold_answer: VOLTA-4 Performance AWD (V4-PF-A) at 230 kW combined, ahead of the ZENITH-11 1.8 L Plug-in Hybrid AT at 220 kW system-combined. A good answer compares all six platforms' variants rather than only the winner's platform.
notes: Exhaustive cross-platform ranking: every platform must be considered; electric and hybrid power is system-combined. Added after a user-reported answer that mentioned only VOLTA-4.

question: Which variant has the longest declared range?
gold_answer: ZENITH-11 2.2 L Diesel AT at 1,120 km (declared combined range), ahead of the ZENITH-11 Plug-in Hybrid at 1,050 km combined and TERRA-9 Mild-Hybrid at 1,010 km.
notes: Exhaustive cross-platform ranking over 21 variants; the PHEV's 1,050 km is the combined figure, not electric-only (72 km) or engine-only (640 km).

question: On a VEGA-7 vehicle built on 15 January 2026, what part number is fitted for the front lower-arm mounting bracket (callout 7), and can the current torque schedule be used to install it?
gold_answer: The vehicle carries the superseded 4471-A bracket (built before the 01 March 2026 cutoff). The current torque schedule for callout 7 (110 ± 10 N·m + 45 deg) applies only to 4471-C; 4471-A was tightened to 95 N·m with no angle stage and applying the 4471-C schedule to it will yield the thread.
notes: Revision-cutoff trap: must flag the build-date cutoff, not just return the current torque value.

question: An ATLAS-6 vehicle was above its GVM limit at the time of failure, but is still within its 3-year/100,000 km coverage and the part is not a wear item. Is the claim approved?
gold_answer: No. The claim is rejected under code R-21. The GVM-overload test is applied first and takes precedence over coverage period and wear-item tests; a covered part on an overloaded vehicle is still rejected.
notes: Order-of-evaluation trap in the adjudication flow (Figure 6.1): GVM overload first.

question: What is NOVA-3's warranty coverage period, and how does it differ from VEGA-7's?
gold_answer: NOVA-3: 2 years or 40,000 km (whichever occurs first). VEGA-7: 3 years or 100,000 km. The NOVA-3 dossier warns the two must not be confused when adjudicating a claim.
notes: Cross-document coverage confusion; defaulting to 3 yr / 100,000 km for NOVA-3 is wrong.

question: Which components in VEGA-7's front suspension assembly (Figure 4.1) changed at Revision C, and which stayed the same?
gold_answer: Only item 7 (front lower-arm mounting bracket, 4471-A to 4471-C) changed at Revision C. Item 9 (compliance bush) is explicitly unchanged and carries part number 4482-L for both configurations.
notes: Load-bearing caption: the unchanged-item statement for item 9 exists in the figure caption, not in a table.

question: Did all homologation tests pass in VEGA-7's Revision C campaign?
gold_answer: No. Three tests failed (HOM-017 door-latch load, HOM-029 pedestrian-head HIC, HOM-038 roof-crush second stage) and two were conditional passes (HOM-066, HOM-068). The campaign was declared closed at 68 of 68 complete because the failures were remediated by the bracket change and re-verified under report ER-2470, which is not reproduced in the dossier. Completed does not mean passed.
notes: Completed vs passed: the headline '68 of 68 completed' must not be reported as all passing.

question: For the TERRA-9 2.2 L Diesel Mild-Hybrid AT, is "the engine's power output" the engine-only figure or the system-combined figure?
gold_answer: Both are reported and they are not interchangeable: engine-only 118 kW @ 3750 rpm and system-combined 125 kW. The combined figure is not available from the engine alone with the 48 V system inactive. The answer must distinguish them (or ask which is meant) rather than pick one.
notes: Engine-only vs system-combined power trap on the mild-hybrid column.

question: How many distinct "range" figures does ZENITH-11's Plug-in Hybrid variant report, and can they be used interchangeably?
gold_answer: Three: electric-only 72 km, engine-only (petrol) 640 km and combined 1,050 km. They are not interchangeable; the electric-only figure must never be given for a combined-range question or vice versa, and the combined figure is not the sum of the other two.
notes: Three-way range trap on the PHEV column.

question: Which VOLTA-4 battery-capacity figure governs driving-range calculations, gross or usable?
gold_answer: The usable capacity (lower than gross). Gross capacity is a manufacturing specification and must not be used to estimate range.
notes: Gross vs usable capacity; both appear in the transposed table on p4 (usable 44.0/58.0/58.0 kWh, gross 47.5/62.0/62.0 kWh).

question: A VOLTA-4 battery degradation claim was adjudicated on 10 January 2026. Should it be assessed against the 65% or 70% SOH threshold?
gold_answer: 65%, the Revision B threshold. The 70% threshold took effect on 22 January 2026 (Revision C); earlier claims keep the superseded 65% figure rather than the current Section 6 rule.
notes: Retroactive threshold trap. Dossier wording (p2): vehicles built before 22 Jan 2026 retain the 65% threshold for claims already open at that date; refer to build/claim date, not document date.

question: A TERRA-9's 48 V battery control module fails at 2 years / 60,000 km. Is this evaluated against the standard 3-year/100,000 km coverage?
gold_answer: No. 48 V battery and control-module claims are first routed to a separate 5-year, unlimited-distance coverage test, independent of the standard 3 yr / 100,000 km coverage, and a claim inside that window goes to a measured state-of-health grading (Table 8.2a) rather than an immediate approve/reject.
notes: HV/48 V battery claims never use the standard mechanical-claim test.

question: Do the ATLAS-6 Dedicated CNG and Diesel Double-Cab variants share the same payload and towing capacity, since they use the same engine block?
gold_answer: No. The Dedicated CNG variant has reduced payload and towing capacity: payload 1,230 kg vs 1,310 kg for the Diesel Double-Cab, and braked towing 2,000 kg vs 2,500 kg, because of the CNG cylinder and its underbed protection frame.
notes: Shared-engine payload trap.

question: Does the NOVA-3 Dedicated CNG variant have a petrol reserve tank like the Bi-fuel CNG variant does?
gold_answer: No. Only the Bi-fuel CNG variant has a small petrol reserve tank (15.0 L); the Dedicated CNG variant has a CNG cylinder only and no petrol tank. Range and tank figures are independent (Bi-fuel 220 km CNG + 195 km petrol reserve; Dedicated 310 km CNG only).
notes: CNG sub-variant fuel-tank trap.

question: A NOVA-3 claim is for a Table 8.2 wear item, but the vehicle is also outside its 2-year/40,000 km coverage. Is it rejected under R-11 (wear item)?
gold_answer: No. Coverage is tested first: the claim is rejected under R-04 (outside coverage), or routed to the Zone Manager under A-21 if a goodwill flag is present on the VIN. R-11 applies to wear items only when the vehicle is within the coverage period.
notes: Wear-item vs out-of-coverage precedence.

question: What is the engine family and displacement of VEGA-7's 1.0 L Turbo Petrol variant, and does it match the other three variants?
gold_answer: Engine family Z10T, displacement 998 cm3. It does not match the others: the 1.2 L Petrol MT, 1.2 L Petrol AMT (engine family K12N) and 1.2 L Bi-fuel CNG (K12N-CNG) all have 1197 cm3.
notes: Transposed-table column discipline; the Turbo column is the third one.

question: Can Appendix A be used to get VOLTA-4's current production SOH threshold or torque specs?
gold_answer: No. Appendix A holds superseded Revision B data retained for traceability only and must not be used for current production, service or regulatory submission; only the figures in the numbered sections govern.
notes: Superseded-appendix exclusion.
